thread:
Marta (eng-platform): Quick sync — we need a concise mapping from pricing plan -> quota bands + burst policy that both the console and billing systems can consume. Current docs are vague and UX is confusing.
Cheng (eng-runtime): Agree. A few edge cases to call out: orgs with multiple API keys, per-key overrides, and 'grace bursts' for new signups.
Oliver (product): For PLG we want free accounts to have a visible, honest burst (eg 5k tok/day) but then a strict softcap. Users should see remaining burst in console.
Jess (pricing): Important: bursts shouldn't count against committed usage for Dedicated customers. Only billed for Hosted after softcap.
Tom (finance): +1 on not double-counting committed capacity. Also need deterministic metrics for invoicing — burst events must be exported as discrete records.
Marta (eng-platform): Proposed mapping draft (simple):
```
{
  "free": {"monthly_quota_tokens": "150000", "burst_allowance_tokens": "5000/day", "burst_throttle": "soft_then-hard"},
  "pro": {"monthly_quota_tokens": "3_000_000", "burst_allowance_tokens": "50_000/day", "burst_throttle": "grace-credits-then-throttle"},
  "enterprise": {"monthly_quota_tokens": "contracted", "burst_allowance_tokens": "contracted", "burst_throttle": "SLA-fallbacks"}
}
```
Cheng (eng-runtime): That's a good start. Need to define semantics: is burst_allowance per-org or per-api-key? If per-org then multiple keys share the pool — simpler for billing. If per-key it's easier for devs to manage keys per feature.
Ali (eng-sre): We should default to per-org with opt-in per-key in console. Per-key would explode telemetry cardinality and make rate-limiter state bigger.
Oliver (product): UX note — if we make bursts per-org, we must surface per-key usage so teams can debug which key burned the burst. Console metric drilldown required.
Jess (pricing): Pricing tie-in: pro plan should include a buffer (eg 10% over quota) billed at discounted overage rate. Free overages cost zero but throttle hard. Enterprise negotiable.
Tom (finance): For invoicing clarity I want "quota buckets" to be recorded as: plan_quota, burst_used, overage_tokens, overage_rate. Each as independent ledger lines.
Marta (eng-platform): Implementation constraints: rate-limiter currently supports token-buckets per-key and per-org. We need an authoritative lookup: plan -> quota bands -> enforcement policy (softcap window length, burst replenish rate, overage_rate).
Cheng (eng-runtime): I'll add an API to the entitlement service returning: {billing_unit, monthly_quota, burst_daily, replenish_rate, enforcement_mode}. Keep it small.
Marta (eng-platform): Console needs mapping table + tooltips. Example tooltip text: "Burst allowance is a short-term buffer above your monthly quota; it is intended for short spikes and will be throttled if abused."
Oliver (product): Also add a clear FAQ that mixing multiple keys doesn't increase quota. That's a common spike vector.
Ali (eng-sre): Question: should we auto-block keys that exceed X large bursts in Y days to prevent abuse? (eg 3 large bursts in 7 days)
Jess (pricing): Yes but call it "abuse detection" and tie to support escalation for enterprise. Free/pro will get automated temporary blocks.
Marta (eng-platform): Operationally we need these outputs for consumers:
- console: human-readable quotas + per-key drilldown
- billing: raw ledger lines per day
- metrics: time series per-org + sample per-key labels (not full cardinality)
Cheng (eng-runtime): Two follow-ups for me: 1) exact JSON contract for entitlement API; 2) how to mark dedicated capacity so runtime exempts it from hosted overage billing.
Tom (finance): We'll need export fields: org_id, plan_id, billing_cycle_start, plan_quota_tokens, burst_tokens_used, overage_tokens, overage_charge_usd.
Marta (eng-platform): Next steps: Cheng to draft entitlement API by EOD tomorrow; Jess to provide overage rates table; Oliver to draft console copy for tooltips and FAQ; Ali to propose abuse thresholds.
Oliver (product): I'll ping design for a compact quota card for the dashboard.
Cheng (eng-runtime): I'll post the API draft in this thread when ready.
billing-bot: billing-bot: New note: remember to add a feature flag for staged rollout for the enforcement changes. :robot_face:
Marta (eng-platform): Good call — feature flag + canary rollout. Also add a console hint when enforcement mode will change (preview).
Jess (pricing): tagging @Tom (finance) for rate approval.
Tom (finance): I'll review rates today. If there are contested cases, prefer simpler billing models for Q1.
Marta (eng-platform): Thanks all — will summarize and create RFC link later.
Cheng (eng-runtime): API draft: posting now (short):
```
GET /entitlements/v1/org/{org_id}
Response:
{
  "plan_id": "pro",
  "monthly_quota_tokens": 3000000,
  "burst_daily_tokens": 50000,
  "replenish_rate_per_sec": 0.58,
  "enforcement_mode": "softcap_then_hard"
}
```
Oliver (product): Nice. One tweak: include "display_quota_tokens" for console-friendly number formatting.
Marta (eng-platform): Closing note: make sure telemetry emits both "quota_exhausted" events and "burst_consumed" samples for downstream alerting. We'll track in the RFC. :white_check_mark:
